title: 1998 AHSME Problem 23
statement: The graphs of \(x^2+y^2=4+12x+6y\) and \(x^2+y^2=k+4x+12y\) intersect when \(k\) satisfies \(a\le k\le b,\) and for no other values of \(k.\) Find \(b-a.\)

solutions.text: The circles are \[ (x-6)^2+(y-3)^2=49, \] \[ (x-2)^2+(y-6)^2=k+40. \] Their centers are \(5\) units apart. With second radius \(r=\sqrt{k+40},\) intersection requires \(|7-r|\le5\le7+r,\) or \(2\le r\le12.\) Thus \(-36\le k\le104,\) and \(b-a=140.\) The correct answer is D.
hints: Complete the square to find both circle centers and radii
Two circles intersect exactly when the center distance lies between the difference and sum of their radii
